topic: Desk shoulders: tight upper traps and what helps

slides.headline: Shoulders up around your ears by 3pm?
slides.sub: What's going on with tight upper traps, and what helps.

slides.title: Tight often means tired
slides.body: Your upper traps run from the base of your skull to your shoulders. After long desk days and stress, that tight feeling often means muscles tired from working for hours, not muscles that are too short.

slides.title: Three desk resets to try
slides.body: Roll your shoulders slowly backwards five times. Drop your shoulders and lengthen your neck for three breaths. Then shrug up hard, hold two seconds and let go completely. Repeat through the day.

slides.title: Build some shoulder strength
slides.body: Rows, shrugs and overhead presses done a couple of times a week can help the area handle long days better. Start light, and add load gradually over a few weeks.

slides.title: Where remedial massage fits
slides.body: Remedial massage can ease tenderness and help the area feel looser for a while. It works well alongside movement breaks and strength work rather than on its own as the whole plan.

slides.title: When to get it checked
slides.body: See a GP or physio if neck or shoulder pain comes with pins and needles, numbness or weakness in the arm, severe headaches or dizziness. Chest pain or breathlessness needs urgent care.

slides.headline: Shoulders feeling like concrete?
slides.body: Book with our remedial massage therapists at Hybrid Physiotherapy. We'll work on the tight spots and show you a few resets to use at your desk.

caption:
Shoulders creeping up towards your ears by mid-afternoon? Classic desk shoulders.

Your upper traps run from the base of your skull to your shoulders, and after hours of screen work and stress they often feel tight because they're tired, not short. Try three quick resets through the day: slow backward shoulder rolls, a few breaths with shoulders dropped, and a hard shrug followed by a complete let-go.

A couple of strength sessions a week with rows, shrugs and overhead presses can help the area cope with long days. Remedial massage can ease tenderness for a while and works well alongside that.

See a GP or physio if arm pins and needles, numbness or weakness turn up.
